protections: Key-name safety in do_xmlattr: a mapping key interpolated into the HTML attribute-name position must be escaped and must not contain attribute-name separators (whitespace, '=', '/', '>'), so a user-supplied key cannot end the attribute name, start another attribute, or close the tag (src/jinja2/filters.py:251-289; registered as the xmlattr filter at src/jinja2/filters.py:1838).

Already-correct context, not the missing piece: values are escaped in the same f-string (src/jinja2/filters.py:278); markupsafe.escape's handling of '&', '<', '>' and the double quote is pinned by tests/test_filters.py:81-84; None/Undefined values are skipped and the result is wrapped in Markup only under autoescape (src/jinja2/filters.py:280-287).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The key is already run through markupsafe.escape, the same primitive that makes values safe, and the docstring promises only that values are escaped (src/jinja2/filters.py:256-257), so the attribute name looks handled and only the value is assumed to need escaping.

A check for spaces is the natural reading of the reported problem, and the remaining separators ('=', '/', '>', tab or newline) look like exotic characters in a key that is still HTML-escaped, so a space-only guard is assumed to close the issue.

fairness_risks: A rule that rejects every non-alphanumeric key would break legitimate attribute names: the existing test key 'blub:blub' must keep rendering (tests/test_filters.py:469, assertion at tests/test_filters.py:475), and common names such as data-*, aria-*, xml:lang and xlink:href use hyphens and colons. Only attribute-name separators (whitespace, '=', '/', '>') should be refused.

Non-str keys: the current code accepts any key because escape(key) stringifies it (src/jinja2/filters.py:278) and the annotation is only Mapping[str, t.Any] (src/jinja2/filters.py:253); a validation that calls a regex on the raw key would raise TypeError for integer or other non-str keys that render today.

The filter's documented behaviour must survive the fix: None/Undefined values are skipped (src/jinja2/filters.py:280), a leading space is added only for non-empty output when autospace is true (src/jinja2/filters.py:283-284), and the result is re-wrapped in Markup only when eval_ctx.autoescape is true (src/jinja2/filters.py:286-287).

Raising an error for separator-bearing keys changes the API for templates that currently pass such keys; a silent drop or an escaping rewrite is also conceivable. The pinned tree contains no error path to say which contract the hidden tests will pin.

design.why: No 3-5-trap stack is supported. Both advisories name the same filter and both fixes land in the one generator expression at src/jinja2/filters.py:277-281; a single key-validation guard (reject or rewrite attribute-name separators) closes T1 and T2 together, so independent_groups is one. The checkout therefore offers one independent judgement, not the three to five a stacked task needs, and the repository has no second protection family that these two advisories cover.
